summary: The agent implemented most of the store maintenance feature: all baseline tests passed and 135 of 137 new tests passed. The two failures are link-identity edge cases in integrity classification.

details.reasoning: The implementation runs and passes the baseline suite plus nearly all maintenance tests, but it does not model ownership and sharing by resolved file identity in all link cases. Its unowned-file scan compares only recorded name strings, so the target of a recorded link is reported as unowned. Its sharesResolvedFile method immediately returns false when resolution is outside the folder, so two entries reaching the same outside file are not recognized as shared and are discarded during repair.
details.secondary_factors: The trajectory shows a peripheral :archunit:check failure while resolving the SpotBugs dependency, but focused compilation and store tests succeeded and the grader completed normally; this did not cause the two graded failures.

justification.issue_description: Link targets are not consistently treated as the file owned or shared by an index entry. The implementation scans unowned files by recorded-name strings and only compares resolved files when both paths pass the in-folder regular-file check.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says that entries whose recorded names resolve to one file are shared, that an entry both shared and something else stays shared, and that repair moves or deletes a link's target with the link. The agent patch at TextFileBasedViolationStore.java lines 326-332 treats only recorded name strings as ownership, while lines 407-409 make sharing impossible when resolvedPath is null; the failing tests are anEntryNamingALinkToAFileInTheStoreOwnsThatFile and twoEntriesReachingOneFileByDifferentNamesShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT because the prompt directly specifies link-target ownership, file-identity sharing, and shared-entry precedence. The agent attempted link handling but its classification algorithm loses the required identity information in these cases; the hidden tests are deterministic checks of explicitly documented behavior, not undocumented conventions.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is dense but specifies the relevant precedence, link, path-safety, repair, fail, and concurrency semantics. The reference implementation confirms the task is solvable, and the two failing tests correspond to explicit requirements rather than unfair hidden assumptions.

evidence: JUnit reports baseline 42/42 passing and new 135/137 passing with two ordinary assertion/initialization failures, not bootstrap or import failures.
The grader completed the Gradle run under JDK 25 and the failures point into TextFileBasedViolationStore.initializeLocked, specifically the agent's integrity behavior.

The trajectory records successful focused store/concurrency verification and compilation. A later broad :archunit:check stopped at spotbugsMain because com.github.spotbugs:spotbugs:4.10.3 could not be resolved, which was peripheral and did not prevent the graded run.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker explains the graded failures; they are reproducible implementation defects in link ownership and sharing classification.

quick_failure_summary: Integrity repair mishandles symlink ownership and shared entries that resolve to the same outside file.
